title: Practice 2: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Mary went to play with Tom.
exercises.why: **пошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». past: он пошёл · она пошла́ · оно пошло́ · они пошли́. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  The other choices: **ходила** is a form of **ходить** (to go, to walk); **шла** is a form of **идти** (to go).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Dan and Linda flew to London.
exercises.why: **полетели** is the past tense (plural) of **полететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the perfective of **лететь**, «set out». past: он полете́л · она полете́ла · оно полете́ло · они полете́ли. — Wiktionary, «полететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The perfective verb полететь (like пойти and поехать) denotes single action with the emphasis on the completed start. The past perfective (полетел, -ла, -ло, -ли) is formed in a regular way. The future perfective (полечу, полетишь) belongs to the 2nd (-и-) type of conjugation. The consonant "т" changes into "ч" in the first person singular only.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лететь — летать: perfective полететь · «for a while» полетать · «round trip» слетать.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Полковник полетел в Вашингтон.» (The Colonel flew to Washington. (single action; completed start)) — DLI, Lesson 55. «Завтра я полечу на фронт.» (Tomorrow I'll fly to the front. (single action)) — DLI, Lesson 55.  The other choices: **летали** is a form of **летать** (to fly); **летели** is a form of **лететь** (to fly, to be flying).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **повёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **повести** (to lead, to conduct, to direct, to drive) — the perfective of **вести**, «set out». past: он повёл · она повела́ · оно повело́ · они повели́. — Wiktionary, «повести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).
